Alex — appreciate you joining. Short technical summary so NetOps has what they need ahead of the workshop. I’ve also uploaded a two-page options brief (redwood_vpc_options.pdf) to the shared Drive link we included in the thread.

What Redwood supports (summary):
Option A — AWS PrivateLink (recommended for strict inbound-only models):
- Redwood creates a PrivateLink endpoint in your VPC; inbound traffic from FinLedger -> Redwood is over the endpoint.
- Egress (outbound from Redwood to external services) can be: (a) Redwood-managed egress IPs (we provide a small stable pool), or (b) customer-managed via a NAT/egress proxy in your VPC if you need absolute ownership.
- Pros: minimal routing changes on your side, better isolation for auditors.
- Cons: Small additional setup on our side and per-endpoint configuration for scaling.

Option B — VPC Peering (recommended if you want direct network-level attachment):
- Low-latency, straightforward routing. Redwood will provide the prefixes we will announce across the peering session.
- Egress model: typically customer-managed NAT -> you retain control of outbound IPs. Redwood can also route egress through our managed NAT if needed.
- Pros: Simpler throughput scaling; Cons: peering across accounts requires careful route table management and may have cross-account limitations.

What we need from FinLedger NetOps before the call:
- Preferred attachment model (PrivateLink or Peering) or "we want Redwood recommendation".
- Staging and prod CIDRs + any ACLs that might block 443/SSL.
- Indication if you require Redwood-managed stable egress IPs or if you will host NAT for outbound traffic. If you require us to provide IPs, share any allowlist format (CIDR or single IP) and rotation windows.
- Contact for the workshop (Alex confirmed) and 2-3 preferred time slots.

Proposed times (Pacific): Tue 11/10 10:00-11:00, Tue 11/10 14:00-15:00, Wed 11/11 09:00-10:00. If those don't work, propose alternatives and we’ll coordinate.

I included a short checklist in the redwood_vpc_options.pdf — it lists ports, sample allowlist CIDRs we can support, and a minimal test plan for staging.
